Bill.BriefDescription: Providing a business and occupation tax credit for certain small business purchases.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to a business and occupation tax credit for smallbusiness; adding a new section to chapter 82.04 RCW; providing aneffective date; and declaring an emergency.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 82.04 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) In computing the tax imposed under this chapter, a credit isallowed for investment in computer equipment by a small business to beused exclusively for business purposes. The credit is equal to thepurchase price of the computer equipment multiplied by ten percent.The credit claimed under this section by a small business may notexceed one hundred dollars for each purchase of computer equipment. (2) The credit must be claimed against taxes due for the samecalendar year in which the computer equipment is purchased. The creditmay not exceed the tax otherwise due under this chapter. A creditearned during a calendar year may not be carried over to be creditedagainst taxes incurred in subsequent calendar years. No refunds may begranted for credits under this section. Credits are available on afirstcome basis. p. 1 HB 1575 (3) No application is necessary for the tax credit. A smallbusiness must electronically file returns with the department ofrevenue to claim the credit under this section and must alsoelectronically file with the department all returns and any other formsor information the department requires in an electronic format asprovided or approved by the department. Any return, form, orinformation required to be filed in an electronic format under thissubsection is not filed until received by the department in anelectronic format. As used in this subsection, "returns" has the samemeaning as "return" in RCW 82.32.050. (4) Small businesses that are on an annual reporting frequency forthe taxes imposed under this chapter may claim the credit provided bythis section at any time prior to the due date of their return in anelectronic format as provided or approved by the department. (5) The department shall keep a running total of all creditsclaimed under this section each fiscal year. The department shall notallow any credits under this section that would cause the total amountof credits claimed in any fiscal year to exceed twenty million dollars. (6) The employment security department shall provide to thedepartment of revenue such information needed by the department ofrevenue to verify eligibility under this section. (7) If at any time the department finds that a person is noteligible for tax credit under this section, the amount of taxes againstwhich a credit was claimed is immediately due and payable. Thedepartment shall assess interest, but not penalties, on the taxesagainst which the credit was claimed. Interest shall be assessed atthe rate provided for delinquent excise taxes under chapter 82.32 RCW,retroactively to the date the credit was claimed, and shall accrueuntil the taxes against which a credit has been claimed are repaid. (8) For purposes of this section, the following definitions apply: (a) "Computer equipment" means personal computers, computersoftware preinstalled on personal computers, keyboards, monitors,printers, and mouse devices. Computer equipment also includes anycomputer peripherals or accessories that operate outside of a personalcomputer when bundled together with a personal computer and sold by theseller as a single product or piece of merchandise. (b) "Small business" means a person as defined in RCW 82.04.030 HB 1575 p. 2 that has fifty or fewer employees. For purposes of this subsection, an"employee" means a fulltime, parttime, or temporary employee coveredby Title 50 RCW for whom the small business is making contributions.
This act is necessary for the immediatepreservation of the public peace, health, or safety, or support of thestate government and its existing public institutions, and takes effectJuly 1, 2005.
